title: Haydn’s Missing Symphony — public composition log
scope: The log the composing agent (Claude) kept while writing this work: the request, its progress messages, the commands it ran on the score and their output, draft publications and test results, up to the publication step. It was written during the work, entry by entry; it is not an automatic export of the whole session, and the same session composed other works whose entries are not included here.
policy: Messages and tool output are recorded as they occurred, shortened where marked. Private internal reasoning, credentials, access details, private paths and unrelated conversation are not included. Statements made during the work may be provisional or mistaken; later corrections remain in the log.

entries.speaker: User
entries.text:
[A long batch brief was pasted: compose and publish one original symphony for each composer in the Missing Works catalogue who has no completed symphony, one composer at a time, claiming each open symphony request through the admin command, publishing live drafts early, testing every movement in the real browser player, writing a notebook and a public composition log, deploying an atomic release, and completing the request only after the public work is verified. Every work must be labelled an original AI-composed homage.]

NOW I know I said to do all composers, but how about we actually do half of the composers in each section? just to save some money.
notes: the pasted batch brief is summarised in brackets; the last sentence is verbatim

entries.speaker: Claude
entries.text:
Composition brief — Haydn’s Missing Symphony (work id haydn-symphony-1)

A four-movement symphony in B flat major in the manner of Haydn’s London symphonies. It is new music: no theme is taken from Haydn, and it is not presented as a lost or rediscovered work.

Orchestra (11 staves, sounding pitch): flute, 2 oboes, 2 bassoons, 2 horns and 2 trumpets in B flat (natural instruments: only notes of their harmonic series), timpani in B flat and F, strings. No clarinets.

Movements
I. Adagio – Allegro. Twelve slow bars that darken to B flat minor, then a sonata-form Allegro that is nearly monothematic, as Haydn’s often are: the main theme returns in F as second subject for the woodwind. The development moves it abruptly to A flat and C minor, runs the transition’s scales through three minor keys, and stages a false reprise in E flat before the real one. Exposition repeated.
II. Adagio cantabile, F major, 3/4: a song for the violins, repeated with flute; a troubled middle section in F minor and A flat; return and short coda. No trumpets or drums.
III. Menuet (B flat) and Trio (E flat, a ländler for solo oboe), with a bar of silence as a joke before the reprise.
IV. Finale: Presto, 2/4, a rondo on a contredanse tune, with an episode in F, a stormy episode in G minor, and pauses that pretend to lose the thread.

Target length about twelve minutes. Compromise known from the start: every tune, the chord plan of every bar and the form are written by hand; a program then scores each passage in one of three textures (quiet strings under a tune, woodwind band, full orchestra), writing the accompaniment figures, the sustained wind chords and the natural brass and drum parts from the chord plan.

entries.speaker: Score build and checks
entries.text: Build m1: write the score, check bar lengths, ranges, sustained notes and half-step clashes, validate with the site validator, compare with abcjs playback, and count parallel fifths/octaves between the outer voices. After fixes: whole-bar rests after the change of metre are written as two half rests (the site's notation library mis-times a whole rest when the opening metre is 3/4); doubled lines are moved by whole octaves instead of note by note; 18 parallel octaves/fifths between tune and bass removed by changing chord inversions and seven melody notes; the flute line in the reprise lowered an octave.

All four movements. Fixes since the first build: held accompaniment notes are now re-struck when the chord changes beneath them (this removed about 25 reported clashes in the Adagio and the Menuet); horn chords in quiet passages are restricted to the natural horn's notes; eight parallel octaves/fifths between tune and bass removed in the Adagio and the Finale.
